findings.summary: Registration-domain lock covers install vs install only; uninstall finalizer checks the registration then deletes it without that lock, so a concurrent same-domain install in another parent can lose its registration
Any failure to open the registration lock is reported as another install being active; distinguish sharing violation from other errors
Win11 prep should list expected residue (registration lock file, retained candidate data root, leftover install-root files) and their cleanup condition
After the formal snapshot comparison, launch the formal install once to observe it still starts

Installer accepts a virtualized (MSIX packaged) LocalAppData while the uninstall finalizer rejects it, creating an instance that installs but cannot uninstall; refuse packaged contexts before any mutation on both sides and run Owner-machine installs in the ordinary view
Uninstall registration-lock failure is not distinguished by Windows error; report 32 as concurrent operation and others by code
Formal 0.1.2 has no HKCU uninstall registration in either view; find the cause and settle the formal install and uninstall path before R2-05
Owner-machine residue (packaged candidate, ordinary lock and data, empty dirs, MC-122 copy, evidence folder) needs an itemised cleanup plan; permanent deletion only with Owner consent
